video.title: Sacramento Kings Fantasy Basketball Preview [26/27 NBA Season]

summary: Josh Lloyd previews the Sacramento Kings for fantasy. He calls them one of the worst teams in the NBA and says the coach, owner and GM make the team very unpredictable. His projected starters are Darius Acuff Jr., Zach LaVine, Keegan Murray, Ben Simmons and Domantas Sabonis. The bench is DeAndre Hunter, Malik Monk, Maxime Raynaud, Precious Achiuwa and Nique Clifford. LaVine is his best target inside the top 100, and he is fine with Sabonis at a higher pick. Murray is fine around pick 90, Acuff is a round 10 flyer, and Simmons is a late rebounds, assists and steals swing. He says to avoid Hunter, Clifford and Cardwell in standard leagues, and to treat Raynaud only as a deep bench stash in weekly or games-cap leagues.

rules.text: On a team likely to finish bottom three, shutting down good veterans can make the team worse and help its pick odds. So the risk for those veterans is a trade more than a tanking shutdown.
rules.quote: shutting him down makes them worse and less likely to have a good pick

rules.text: Rookie guards are usually bad for fantasy unless they are elite prospects. Treat them as late flyers.
rules.quote: rookies are pretty notoriously bad. Rookie guards are pretty notoriously bad.

rules.text: Do not trust high preseason usage numbers from rookies to last through the season.
rules.quote: I don't really believe that 31 usage will be a realistic number for him as we move through the season.

rules.text: Rookies and inefficient scorers can be worth more in points leagues than in category leagues. Lean into them more in points leagues.
rules.quote: pretty big discrepancies between his category and points league value

rules.text: Do not draft a backup who needs a trade or injury to the starter in a standard daily league. NBA trades mostly happen at the February deadline, so you would hold a low-value player for months.
rules.quote: realistically, when do trades happen in the NBA? At the deadline, February.

rules.text: Stash-type backups only make sense in games-cap, draft-only, deep bench weekly leagues.
rules.quote: games cap draft only deep bench weekly league stash waiting in case Sabonis gets hurt

rules.text: Late-season stats from bad teams are inflated because opponents are not trying. Discount them.
rules.quote: start going balls out in March when no one else was trying. So, a lot of their numbers are inflated.

rules.text: Players who post big numbers only when everyone in front of them is injured need volume. Do not chase them when the rotation is healthy.
rules.quote: when you were playing on a team when nobody is there, which is what happened

player_notes.text: He faded Sabonis last season because guards needed the ball. Simmons starting next to him this season makes him a bit more cautious.
player_notes.quote: the Simmons starting group situation makes me a little bit more cautious about it

player_notes.text: Sabonis finished 61st in category leagues and 45th in points leagues last season. ESPN ADP is 19 and Yahoo ADP is 29. He could be top 25 in categories and top 20 in points.
player_notes.quote: I think he could easily be a top 20 points league player and a top 25 category player.

player_notes.text: Sabonis had multiple injuries last season, including a meniscus issue that ended in surgery. He played under 30 minutes after 35 to 36 the two seasons before.
player_notes.quote: He played under 30 minutes a night after being at 35 and 36 the two previous seasons.

player_notes.text: He can see Sabonis back over 6 assists, 55% shooting, 23 to 24 usage and 33 minutes. That would make him a top 30 player.
player_notes.quote: I can see him getting back 23 to 24 usage and playing 33 minutes. And that's a top 30 guy.

player_notes.text: The main worry is a trade to a team where Sabonis plays a Vucevic-level backup role.
player_notes.quote: The worry is more trade to me on a team where he goes and plays a Vevich level backup role.

player_notes.text: Sabonis is healthy now. He has played in the preseason.
player_notes.quote: Sabonas had the knee issue um last season, but he's fine. He's played in the preseason.

player_notes.text: LaVine shoots elite percentages and can add around 4.5 assists when he has the ball. His assists drop when others handle it.
player_notes.quote: Part of Lavine's appeal back in Chicago was he'd be a guy that would shoot elite percentages

player_notes.text: LaVine was 110th last season. His Yahoo ADP is around 102, and ESPN has him at 159. He is happily drafting LaVine inside the top 100 and is not worried about the finger injury.
player_notes.quote: ESPN's got him at 159. Ludicrous. I'm happily grabbing him inside the top 100.

player_notes.text: LaVine is one of the best targets on the team. He likes grabbing LaVine quite late.
player_notes.quote: I think one of the best targets is Zack Lavine. I'm not I'm not going to go super in on it

player_notes.text: Murray has shot poorly from three every season since his rookie year. His usage has never reached 20.
player_notes.quote: He also was horrendous from three, shooting 41% as a rookie down to 36, 34, and 28 last season.

player_notes.text: Murray was 100th in points leagues last season, and ESPN ranks him 83. He doubts the 1.6 blocks will hold with Simmons playing. He is okay drafting Murray around pick 90, with upside to about 60th.
player_notes.quote: I do like taking him late. I think that he he's falling in quite a few different drafts

player_notes.text: Acuff has 31 usage in preseason, averaging 19 points and 4 assists in 26 minutes while hitting 41% from three. He projects outside the top 170. Take him around round 10 as a flyer, with more value in points leagues.
player_notes.quote: my projections don't even have him top 170, but that's okay. Who cares? Take him in

player_notes.text: Simmons cannot shoot and has very low usage. He offers rebounds, assists and steals and plays good defense. He doubts his body can handle 60 games.
player_notes.quote: I'm not even sure his body can handle playing 60 games.

player_notes.text: Simmons is projected to start. He is a late category-league swing for a 6/6/6 type line.
player_notes.quote: So if you want to take him late, do it. But it's the 666.

player_notes.text: Hunter comes off the bench. He was 248th last season, and his Yahoo ADP of 91 makes no sense. He calls him a 20-team-league player only and says not to touch him.
player_notes.quote: Just don't touch him. This is a 20 team league guy, especially if he's not going to be starting.

player_notes.text: Monk would be rostered everywhere at 27 minutes a night, but he might get DNPs again. He thinks the team hates him, and he is only a 14 to 16 team league option.
player_notes.quote: Malik Monk, I don't think we drive Monk outside of like 14 to 16 teams.

player_notes.text: Raynaud was 156th in category leagues while starting 56 games at 30 minutes. He is a backup to Sabonis and is coming off a knee injury. Drafting him in standard formats makes no sense.
player_notes.quote: Drafting Maxim Reno in a standard format makes no sense.

player_notes.text: Raynaud helps in FG% and FT% as a big man, but he never blocks shots.
player_notes.quote: He's the big man who can get you 60 and 80 from the field goal and free throw percentage categories.

player_notes.text: Raynaud suffered a patella subluxation. He should miss a couple of weeks and might miss week one.
player_notes.quote: They called it a patella subluxation. So it looks like he'll be okay a couple of weeks

player_notes.text: Achiuwa was 187th last season. He should be the backup center and is a short-term deep league target. He offers rebounds and FG%, but his free throws are bad.
player_notes.quote: So, in deeper formats, you can consider him a draftable target, at least for the short term

player_notes.text: Clifford is in the rotation but very inconsistent. He is a good steals player, but there is no need for interest this season.
player_notes.quote: Clifford is like absolutely not. Like he needed like 40 minutes a night, everyone out to do something.

player_notes.text: Sharp is a name to watch as a high-steals, decent-shooting backup point guard. Monk is still ahead of him.
player_notes.quote: Emanuel Sharp is a name to watch. a really high steals and decent shooting backup point guard.

player_notes.text: Cardwell has a calf strain and is the third or fourth string center. Do not bother stashing him.
player_notes.quote: So don't bother with Cardwell. I know the immediate reaction was Raino's out.

team_notes.text: The Kings are one of the worst teams in the NBA, with poor coaching, ownership and front office. That makes their rotations unpredictable.
team_notes.quote: it's a team with the worst coach in the NBA, the worst owner in the NBA

team_notes.text: The projected starters are Acuff, LaVine, Murray, Simmons and Sabonis.
team_notes.quote: Darius Akov Jr. Zack Lavine Keegan Murray Ben Simmons and Dantis Sabonis.

team_notes.text: The projected bench is Hunter, Monk, Raynaud, Achiuwa and Clifford.
team_notes.quote: the bench five will include DeAndre Hunter, Malik Monk, Maxim Reo, the Big Sneeze, Precious Aure

team_notes.text: Two of the five bigs are injured to start the season, so Achiuwa and a two-way big get the backup minutes.
team_notes.quote: And two of those five are injured to start the season.

team_notes.text: Schedule: 4-4-3 if your league ends March 28, or 4-3-4 if it ends April 4. That is 11 games and 14 back-to-backs.
team_notes.quote: If you end on March 28th, it's a 443. If you end on April 4th, it's a 4-34.
